observations.body: The Spirit immediately drives Jesus into the wilderness. He is there forty days, tempted by Satan, with wild animals, while angels serve him.
observations.label: Mark compresses wilderness, Satan, animals, and angels

payload.posture: Read Mark 1:12–13 as one movement in the temptation of Jesus, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states the Spirit immediately drives Jesus into the wilderness. He is there forty days, tempted by Satan, with wild animals, while angels serve him. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of the temptation of Jesus.
payload.title: Mark compresses wilderness, Satan, animals, and angels
